question: A child is forced to weave in a dark room for twelve hours daily. What category of trafficking is this?

options.A: Commercial sex trade
options.B: Illegal adoption
options.C: Domestic servitude
options.D: Forced child labor

explanation: Working long hours in production or hazardous trades falls under forced child labor rather than house chores. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T25#GNS225_U5_T25_h3)

question: What do we call a loss that can be clearly seen and verified by everyone around, like losing a limb or a loved one?

options.A: A loss that is only felt internally by the affected individual
options.B: A loss of money or property caused by economic changes
options.C: A loss that occurs only during old age and natural retirement
options.D: A loss that can be recognized and verified by other people

explanation: Spot on! An actual loss is tangible. It's something both the patient and outsiders can clearly see, touch, or acknowledge, like an amputation or death. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T9#GNS321_U4_T9_h1)

question: When is a nebulizer most commonly chosen over a metered-dose inhaler?

options.A: When the patient needs a device that fits easily in a small shirt pocket
options.B: When treatment must be completed in less than five seconds
options.C: When the patient cannot coordinate deep breathing with a handheld inhaler
options.D: When the healthcare provider wants to avoid using any electricity or gas

explanation: Nebulizers produce a continuous mist over several minutes, making them great for young children, the elderly, or acutely breathless patients. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h3)

question: What should a nurse manager do if they check the results and realize a new decision isn't working out?

options.A: Permanently stop evaluating all ward outcomes
options.B: Ignore the data and pretend everything is fine
options.C: Tweak the approach or pivot to a new strategy
options.D: Blame the junior nursing staff for sabotage

explanation: Evaluation is there to guide you. If a strategy falls short, a great leader adjusts their sails rather than ignoring reality. [learn more](GST321_U1_T8#GST321_U1_T8_h7)

question: How does the sympathetic nervous system affect your pupils?

options.A: It causes dilation to let in more light
options.B: It causes involuntary blinking movements
options.C: It causes constriction to protect the retina
options.D: It has no direct effect on pupil size

explanation: When danger strikes, your pupils widen (dilate) so you can take in more visual details of your surroundings. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T30#GNS211_U3_T30_h5)

question: You cover an open surgical wound with a sterile dressing. Which part of the infection chain are you primarily blocking?

options.A: Infectious agent
options.B: Infectious reservoir
options.C: Portal of entry
options.D: Portal of exit

explanation: Well done! A sterile dressing acts like a shield, stopping new germs from getting into the vulnerable, open tissue. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the main goal of taking lifelong antiretroviral therapy (ART) for HIV?

options.A: To completely eliminate all dietary restrictions
options.B: To prevent the need for any future clinic visits
options.C: To successfully suppress the viral load
options.D: To permanently boost red blood cell counts

explanation: Keep it up! Taking medications daily keeps the virus under control, which protects the immune system and stops further transmission. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T6#GNS216_U6_T6_h3)

question: Why do nurses take a detailed health history when assessing a patient's blood (haematological) health?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial cost of patient care
options.B: To catch subtle clues about blood and clotting abnormalities
options.C: To diagnose the exact type of cancer immediately
options.D: To replace the need for routine laboratory blood tests

explanation: Spotting early clues in a patient's history helps you catch blood and clotting issues before they become serious. Great job thinking like a nurse! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T2#GNS311_U2_T2_h1)

question: A family member is feeding a stroke survivor who can actually hold a spoon with an adaptive grip. What should you do?

options.A: Recommend switching the patient entirely to liquid nutritional supplements
options.B: Praise the family member for providing thorough and efficient care
options.C: Insist that the nurse take over all feeding duties moving forward
options.D: Encourage the patient to use the adaptive spoon independently during meals

explanation: We always want to cheer patients on to do as much as they can for themselves. Independence speeds up recovery! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T9#GNS324_U4_T9_h3)

question: What do we call it when blood collects inside the pleural space?

options.A: Pneumothorax
options.B: Empyema
options.C: Hemothorax
options.D: Pleural effusion

explanation: You got it! 'Hemo' means blood and 'thorax' means chest, so blood in the chest cavity is a hemothorax. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T18#GNS221_U2_T18_h2)

question: What is the main reason we give folic acid supplements to women in early pregnancy?

options.A: To accelerate infant tooth eruption
options.B: To lower maternal blood pressure
options.C: To prevent neural tube defects
options.D: To stop excessive morning sickness

explanation: Folic acid taken before and during early pregnancy helps protect the baby's developing brain and spinal cord. Super important vitamin! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h6)

question: Why do nurses closely monitor blood potassium levels in patients taking loop diuretics?

options.A: Loop diuretics cause the body to lose potassium in the urine
options.B: Potassium prevents the patient from developing a dry cough
options.C: Potassium levels determine the correct dose of furosemide
options.D: High potassium levels stop the diuretic from working completely

explanation: Spot on! Loop diuretics flush out water, but they drag important potassium along with it. Keeping an eye on labs helps us prevent dangerous low potassium (hypokalemia). [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is a direct consequence of having weak vital data collection systems in a country?

options.A: Doctors will have less paperwork to complete daily
options.B: Citizens will stop falling sick from infectious diseases
options.C: Hospitals will automatically receive excess funding
options.D: Health planners rely on estimates that may lead to poor interventions

explanation: Inaccurate or missing data forces decision-makers to guess where resources are needed, resulting in poorly targeted health programs. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h6)

question: Which body organ is mainly responsible for breaking down most oral cough medications?

options.A: Spleen
options.B: Liver
options.C: Pancreas
options.D: Kidneys

explanation: The liver is our chemical processing plant—it breaks down oral drugs using special enzymes before the body clears them. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T1#GNS223_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why is dobutamine often prescribed for a patient with cardiogenic shock?

options.A: It strengthens the pumping action of the heart muscle
options.B: It prevents dangerous allergic reactions in the blood
options.C: It removes excess fluid directly through the kidneys
options.D: It lowers the patient's body temperature to rest the heart

explanation: Dobutamine is an inotrope that increases the force of myocardial contraction, helping a weak heart pump more blood forward. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h6)

question: Which layer of the heart wall does the actual hard work of pumping blood?

options.A: Pericardium
options.B: Endocardium
options.C: Myocardium
options.D: Epicardium

explanation: The myocardium is made of strong muscle tissue. Every time your heart beats, it's the myocardium doing the heavy lifting to push blood out! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h2)

question: How should a nurse safely feed a baby admitted with active neonatal tetanus?

options.A: Administering intravenous nutrition exclusively for weeks
options.B: Encouraging frequent and forceful oral suckling
options.C: Using a nasogastric or orogastric tube
options.D: Using an open cup held against the lower lip

explanation: You got it! Trying to feed by mouth can trigger dangerous jaw spasms and choke the baby, making tube feeding the safest choice. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T018#GNS226_U3_T018_h6)

question: A patient tells a nurse they want to stop taking their pills because of minor nausea. What is a key way a support group can help?

options.A: By sharing practical tips on how peers managed similar side effects and survived them
options.B: By replacing the prescribed antiretroviral drugs with local herbal teas
options.C: By providing free over-the-counter antibiotics to cure the HIV infection completely
options.D: By allowing the patient to take a permanent break from treatment without oversight

explanation: Hearing from others who successfully pushed through early side effects gives patients the courage to stay on treatment. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h3)

question: What is the primary focus of critical care nursing in the ICU?

options.A: Conducting long-term physical therapy and rehabilitation exercises
options.B: Providing continuous monitoring and specialized care for life-threatening problems
options.C: Managing basic daily hygiene and routine oral medication schedules
options.D: Discharging stable patients back to their primary care providers

explanation: Critical care nursing is specifically designed for patients with life-threatening conditions who need close observation and advanced interventions. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which principle of nutritional guidance means avoiding the overconsumption of specific nutrients like fats and sodium?

options.A: Isolation
options.B: Moderation
options.C: Adequacy
options.D: Balance

explanation: Moderation refers to keeping intake within appropriate limits to avoid consuming too much of things like fat, sugar, or salt. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h3)

question: Why do nurses collect clinical specimens like urine or wound swabs from sick patients?

options.A: To lower the patient's body temperature during a high fever
options.B: To test the cleaning strength of hospital floor soap
options.C: To replace lost fluids in the patient's bloodstream
options.D: To allow the laboratory to isolate and identify the exact pathogen causing illness

explanation: You nailed it! Lab specimens help find the exact germ making the patient sick so doctors can choose the right medicine. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h7)

question: Why must a nurse keep a strict 'chain of custody' when handling forensic evidence?

options.A: To ensure the collected evidence is legally admissible in court
options.B: To reduce hospital supply and inventory costs
options.C: To diagnose underlying sexually transmitted infections faster
options.D: To speed up the patient's physical recovery process

explanation: Keeping strict track of who handles evidence stops it from getting lost or tampered with so it can actually help get justice in court. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T13#GNS312_U4_T13_h3)

question: Why is keeping girls in school considered a powerful community-level defense against early marriage?

options.A: Academic settings prevent girls from ever interacting with families
options.B: Schools provide free housing for all married minors
options.C: Government laws fine parents who do not send boys to school
options.D: Education delays marriage and equips girls with economic independence skills

explanation: Education empowers girls with knowledge, raises their self-esteem, and naturally pushes the age of marriage higher. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h6)

question: What is the best first step when walking into the hospital room of a patient with a visual impairment?

options.A: Stand quietly by the bed until they notice you.
options.B: Touch their shoulder gently to grab their attention.
options.C: State your name and role clearly before approaching.
options.D: Turn on all the room lights to maximum brightness.

explanation: Spot on! Always use your voice first so you don't startle them since they cannot see you enter the room. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T13#GNS324_U4_T13_h3)

question: How do mass movements differ from regular mixing movements in the large intestine?

options.A: Segmental movements require conscious effort to move waste.
options.B: Segmental contractions happen only once or twice a day.
options.C: Mass movements push stool a long way toward the rectum all at once.
options.D: Mass movements happen non-stop all day and night.

explanation: Mass movements are like big, powerful waves that sweep through the colon every now and then to clear out stored waste toward the exit. You've got this! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h1)

question: How do unregulated herbal remedies often contribute to chronic kidney disease in clinical practice?

options.A: By lowering systemic blood pressure so drastically that blood stops flowing
options.B: By stimulating the overproduction of red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.C: By causing sudden dehydration that increases daily urine output permanently
options.D: By introducing heavy metals and toxic substances that damage the kidney tubules

explanation: As nurses, we see this often. Many traditional concoctions contain hidden toxins that gradually injure the delicate filtering structures of the kidneys over long periods of use. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h2)

question: Why do nurses keep their feet wide apart when lifting a patient?

options.A: To reduce pressure on the knees
options.B: To create a stable base of support
options.C: To stretch the hamstring muscles
options.D: To increase speed during the transfer

explanation: Spreading your feet gives you great balance and keeps you steady, so you don't easily lose your footing while helping a patient. You've got this! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h1)

question: What special connections link heart muscle cells together so they can beat in a coordinated rhythm?

options.A: Neuromuscular junctions
options.B: Sarcoplasmic reticula
options.C: Intercalated discs
options.D: Gap-free desmosomes

explanation: Intercalated discs act like special communication highways between heart cells, letting electrical signals pass instantly so the heart pumps as one team! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T8#GNS121_U3_T8_h3)

question: How often should a bedbound patient ideally be repositioned to prevent pressure injuries?

options.A: Only when the patient complains
options.B: Once every twelve hours
options.C: At least every two hours
options.D: Once per day during the morning shift

explanation: Turning or repositioning a patient every two hours relieves continuous pressure on vulnerable skin areas and tissues. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h6)

question: A woman who had FGM as a child comes in for delivery. What major complication is she most at risk for?

options.A: Complete absence of uterine contractions throughout the first stage
options.B: Obstructed labor due to severe scar tissue and rigid tissue narrowing
options.C: Sudden development of gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Premature closure of the infant's fontanelles inside the womb

explanation: Spot on! Thick scar tissue from FGM doesn't stretch easily, making it very hard for the baby to pass through smoothly during childbirth. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T1#GNS312_U1_T1_h2)

question: What are the three core functions of public health?

options.A: Inpatient care, pharmacy, and laboratory
options.B: Planning, budgeting, and marketing
options.C: Assessment, policy development, and assurance
options.D: Diagnosis, surgery, and rehabilitation

explanation: The recognized framework for public health activities consists of assessment, policy development, and assurance. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is a key focus of antenatal care specifically for pregnant teenagers?

options.A: Nutritional support and close monitoring for anemia and hypertension
options.B: Encouraging unassisted home deliveries to lower hospital costs
options.C: Avoiding all physical exercise throughout the entire pregnancy
options.D: Strict community isolation to avoid social stigma and gossip

explanation: Correct! Since teens are still growing themselves, they need extra nutrition and close checks for blood pressure and iron levels. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h5)

question: What is the primary focus of nursing when promoting wellness along the continuum?

options.A: Empowering patients through education, support, and holistic assessment
options.B: Directing patients to ignore lifestyle factors and rely only on drugs
options.C: Controlling all aspects of a patient's personal daily routine
options.D: Solely diagnosing medical diseases and prescribing surgical treatments

explanation: Nurses focus on helping patients understand their bodies and adopt healthy habits to move toward wellness. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h5)

question: A stroke damages the motor tracts on the right side of a patient's brain. Where will they likely show physical weakness?

options.A: Exclusively in the respiratory diaphragm
options.B: Only in the facial muscles on the right side
options.C: Equally on both sides of the entire body
options.D: On the left side of the body

explanation: Because our motor pathways cross over to the opposite side, brain damage on the right side causes weakness on the left side of the body. Classic nursing neurology! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T16#GNS211_U3_T16_h7)

question: Why is watching a patient's brain function so important after heart tumour surgery?

options.A: The brain stops receiving oxygen if the patient lies flat
options.B: Tumour fragments or tiny clots could dislodge during surgery and cause a stroke
options.C: Patients with heart surgery always develop sudden memory loss
options.D: Anesthesia permanently damages the brain's visual cortex

explanation: Working inside the heart chambers can accidentally send tiny bits of debris or clots up to the brain. Neurological checks help nurses catch a stroke early! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T8#GNS213_U1_T8_h7)

question: Why can blocking dopamine in the tuberoinfundibular pathway lead to higher prolactin levels?

options.A: Prolactin is converted into dopamine in the bloodstream
options.B: Dopamine directly stimulates the pituitary gland to produce milk
options.C: Blockade destroys the cells that store prolactin
options.D: Dopamine normally acts to inhibit prolactin release

explanation: Normally, dopamine acts like a brake on prolactin. When antipsychotics block that dopamine, you take the brake off, and prolactin levels rise. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h2)

question: When is it legally and ethically okay for a nurse to share a patient's confidential abuse details?

options.A: At any time the nurse feels curious about the case details
options.B: When there is a mandatory legal requirement or imminent danger to life
options.C: Whenever family members demand information about the incident
options.D: When posting general hospital statistics on social media

explanation: Spot on! Patient privacy is sacred, but we must break confidentiality if someone's life is in immediate danger or the law requires mandatory reporting. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T8#GNS312_U4_T8_h8)

question: What is the medical term for a young girl's very first menstrual period?

options.A: Menopause
options.B: Menarche
options.C: Mittelschmerz
options.D: Dysmenorrhea

explanation: Well done! Menarche is simply the medical word for that first major milestone of monthly bleeding during puberty. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h3)

question: A patient with severe nerve pain after shingles is given an anticonvulsant. Why?

options.A: To lower systemic blood pressure and reduce cardiac workload
options.B: To destroy the viral infection causing the localized skin rash
options.C: To calm hyperactive nerve impulses transmitting abnormal pain signals
options.D: To completely replace the need for any physical therapy sessions

explanation: Damaged nerves love to fire random, painful zaps. Anticonvulsants quiet those wild nerve signals right down. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T1#GNS223_U5_T1_h5)

question: How should a nurse view a patient's relapse during long-term addiction recovery?

options.A: As definitive proof that the patient will never recover
options.B: As an indicator that the treatment plan needs adjustment
options.C: As a personal moral failure by the individual
options.D: As a minor event that requires no change in clinical care

explanation: Addiction is a chronic relapsing condition, meaning a return to use signals that support strategies or medications need re-evaluation. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h8)

question: A community health nurse in a rural Nigerian village organizes an outreach to teach mothers how to mix oral rehydration salts for diarrhea. What type of intervention is this?

options.A: A purely administrative task unrelated to patient welfare
options.B: A tertiary action meant exclusively for chronic surgical patients
options.C: An unnecessary hospital procedure reserved only for intensive care units
options.D: A practical community-level nursing intervention promoting health recovery

explanation: Community outreach brings essential health knowledge directly to where people live to prevent severe illness. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h6)

question: How is the daily amount of protein on a restricted diet typically calculated?

options.A: Percentage of total daily fluid intake
options.B: Cups per gallon of water consumed
options.C: Ounces per meal regardless of size
options.D: Grams per kilogram of body weight

explanation: Dietary protein prescriptions are personalized to the patient's body mass to ensure they receive enough for basic needs without overloading their organs. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h3)

question: Why does practicing assertiveness help reduce workplace burnout in nursing?

options.A: It forces hospital management to increase your salary
options.B: It guarantees that you will never work night shifts
options.C: It stops doctors from ever questioning your care plan
options.D: It prevents unvoiced frustrations from building up

explanation: Voicing concerns early stops resentment and chronic stress from overwhelming your mental health. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h3)

question: Which type of vaccine contains a weakened form of a live germ?

options.A: Inactivated
options.B: Live-attenuated
options.C: Recombinant
options.D: Toxoid

explanation: Spot on! 'Live-attenuated' means a living germ has been weakened (attenuated) so it can safely spark a strong immune response. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h2)

question: A patient scheduled for a CT scan with contrast says they have a severe allergy to shellfish. What should you do first?

options.A: Proceed with the scan because shellfish has no link to dye
options.B: Encourage the patient to drink extra water for one hour
options.C: Administer an oral dose of calcium supplements right away
options.D: Notify the healthcare provider immediately before the test

explanation: Shellfish allergies often overlap with iodine-based contrast allergies. Always alert the doctor right away so they can order premedication or choose a safer option. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h7)

question: If you check the blood pressure of a patient with Addison's disease, what are you most likely to find?

options.A: Normal blood pressure
options.B: Low blood pressure
options.C: High blood pressure
options.D: Fluctuating high pressure

explanation: Without enough aldosterone, the body loses too much salt and water. Less fluid in the pipes means low blood pressure (hypotension). Makes complete sense when you trace the plumbing! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T3#GNS222_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why are older adults much more prone to chronic dehydration?

options.A: Kidneys produce excessive water during the night.
options.B: The natural sensation of thirst decreases with age.
options.C: Older adults require zero fluids to maintain normal health.
options.D: The skin absorbs all environmental moisture instantly.

explanation: Spot on! As people grow older, their internal thirst signals get quieter, meaning they might not feel thirsty even when their body is crying out for water. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T1#GNS324_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the main difference between the two sides of the Loop of Henle?

options.A: The descending limb performs active secretion, while the ascending limb performs filtration.
options.B: The descending limb is permeable to water, while the ascending limb is impermeable to water.
options.C: The descending limb receives blood supply, while the ascending limb holds lymph fluid.
options.D: The descending limb pumps out salt, while the ascending limb absorbs extra water.

explanation: You got it! Water flows out easily on the way down, but on the way up, the tube lets out salt without letting water follow. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T6#GNS121_U2_T6_h5)

question: A patient asks you (the nurse) to hang out after they leave the hospital. Why is this a bad idea?

options.A: It proves the patient is trying to manipulate hospital administration
options.B: It shows the nurse has not documented patient care properly in the chart
options.C: It violates the rule that therapeutic relationships have a defined professional end
options.D: It means the patient has completely failed to recover from their illness

explanation: Professional care must end when the patient heals. Crossing over into a personal friendship blurs professional boundaries and isn't allowed. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the body's main use for carbohydrates?

options.A: Building structural support for internal organs
options.B: Acting as cofactors for enzyme production
options.C: Transporting fat-soluble vitamins through blood
options.D: Providing a quick and primary source of energy

explanation: Spot on! Carbs break down easily into glucose, giving your body and brain the fast fuel needed to power through the day. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T002#GNS227_U4_T002_h2)

question: Which dangerous bacterial infection can easily enter through an open Guinea worm wound if someone isn't vaccinated?

options.A: Typhoid fever
options.B: Tetanus
options.C: Plague
options.D: Cholera

explanation: Well done! Open skin sores exposed to dirt are prime entry points for tetanus spores. This is why wound care and vaccination history matter so much in nursing! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h7)

question: Why is a luminal medication also prescribed along with tissue-active drugs?

options.A: To replace lost electrolytes and boost red blood cell production
options.B: To permanently numb the lining of the stomach against acid
options.C: To speed up the healing of skin lesions on the abdomen
options.D: To clear remaining cysts from the bowel lumen and prevent relapse

explanation: Exactly! While one drug clears the tissues, the luminal agent mops up any cysts left in the gut so the infection doesn't bounce back. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h5)

question: What procurement practice helps health authorities buy essential medicines at a much lower cost?

options.A: Bulk purchasing using generic non-proprietary names
options.B: Ordering exclusively through expensive luxury suppliers
options.C: Importing only patented brand-name formulations
options.D: Buying small batches from local retail pharmacies daily

explanation: Great job! Buying large quantities of generics lets health systems take advantage of bulk discounts. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h6)

question: How do you properly test Cranial Nerve VII (the Facial nerve)?

options.A: By asking the patient to identify different sweet and salty tastes
options.B: By observing facial symmetry while the patient smiles and frowns
options.C: By checking if the tongue stays straight when sticking it out
options.D: By testing the corneal blink reflex using a cotton wisp

explanation: Since CN VII controls facial expressions, watching if both sides of the face move evenly when they smile or frown is the best test! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h4)

question: If a patient has severe anemia with very low hemoglobin, what is the most direct problem this causes?

options.A: Complete cessation of carbon dioxide production
options.B: Reduced oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood
options.C: Inability of the diaphragm to contract properly
options.D: Immediate collapse of alveolar air sacs

explanation: Spot on! Fewer delivery trucks (hemoglobin) mean the blood just can't pack and carry enough oxygen to the body tissues. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T1#GNS213_U2_T1_h5)

question: How should the normal esophagus appear on a healthy barium swallow image?

options.A: A wide pouch with multiple jagged blockages
options.B: A rigid, non-moving tube with thickened walls
options.C: A smooth, straight tubular structure with uniform width
options.D: A completely closed channel with zero contrast entry

explanation: A healthy esophagus shows an even, smooth column of barium moving down without unusual narrowing, widening, or pouching. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of data interpretation in nursing research?

options.A: To hide negative results from hospital administrators and staff
options.B: To collect as many patient surveys as possible without analysis
options.C: To make sure every research study costs less money to run
options.D: To turn raw research findings into meaningful conclusions for care

explanation: Data interpretation translates raw numbers and notes into clear findings that nurses can use to improve patient care. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T3#GNS224_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core ethical principle guiding palliative nursing care?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Beneficence
options.C: Punitive dominance
options.D: Non-maleficence

explanation: Punitive dominance is made up! Nursing ethics are built on principles like autonomy, beneficence, and non-maleficence. Easy point for you! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T11#GNS321_U4_T11_h6)

question: A postnatal mother comes in with a fever and foul-smelling lochia. What does this usually mean?

options.A: Early return of normal menstruation
options.B: Normal involution of the uterus
options.C: Dehydration from breastfeeding
options.D: Postnatal sepsis or infection

explanation: Bad-smelling lochia combined with a fever is a classic red flag for a uterine infection. You'll want to escalate this quickly for medical treatment! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h2)

question: Which action represents the correct use of alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: Applying the rub and wiping the hands dry quickly with a cloth towel
options.B: Applying the rub and rubbing hands together until the solution is completely dry
options.C: Rinsing the hands with clean water right after applying the rub
options.D: Applying the rub only when wearing sterile surgical gloves

question: What happens to natural cortisol production when a patient takes high-dose steroids for a long time?

question: What should a nurse do if they inspect a wound and notice the edges are still gaping apart?

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to accessing social services for special children in Nigeria?

question: What should you do if asked to perform a task outside your training and scope of practice?

options.A: Decline the task based on your scope of practice

options.C: Pretend you completed the task on the patient's chart
options.D: Ask a patient to teach you how to do it

question: What is the main muscle cell that makes up the heart wall?

question: What is the primary function of the large intestine during digestion?

options.A: Absorbing water and electrolytes

options.D: Producing digestive enzymes

question: What was a major focus of early community health efforts during the colonial days in Nigeria?

options.A: Exporting medical equipment overseas

question: How does external radiation therapy mainly work to destroy cancer cells?

question: What is the main reason clinical instructors use direct observation?

question: What is a common reason why refugee parents might arrange an early marriage for their teenage daughter during a crisis?

question: Why is supporting family members such an important part of critical care nursing?

question: What is an obstetric fistula?

options.A: A permanent infection of the surgical wound after a caesarean section
options.B: A complete blockage of the fallopian tubes caused by gonorrhea
options.C: A chronic weakness of the heart muscle following severe pre-eclampsia
options.D: An abnormal hole between the birth canal and bladder or rectum

question: A patient comes to the clinic with ongoing pelvic pain and high anxiety, and hints point toward past abuse. What does this show us?

question: Why is it tricky that many STIs in women show no symptoms at all?

options.C: Routine diagnostic tests consistently fail to detect silent infections

question: Why are interdisciplinary rounds (where different health workers meet together) so helpful?

options.C: They remove the need for any documentation in the patient chart

explanation: Brilliant! Bringing everyone together at once clears up confusion instantly so the whole healthcare team is on the exact same page for the patient. [learn more](GST321_U1_T12#GST321_U1_T12_h4)

question: What does the Latin name 'dura mater' mean in plain English?

question: What should a nurse focus on when assessing a pregnant patient for constipation?

question: During a hospital admission assessment, what is a vital detail to find out about a patient's substance history?

question: When is the best time to give antiemetic (anti-nausea) medication to a palliative patient who struggles with nausea at meal times?

options.A: Right before bedtime
options.B: Only when the patient falls asleep
options.C: Right after finishing a large plate
options.D: Before meals

explanation: Well reasoned! Giving the anti-nausea medicine ahead of time stops nausea before it starts, helping the patient actually enjoy a few bites of food. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T17#GNS321_U4_T17_h3)

question: What is the traditional foundation for caring for the sick and elderly in Nigerian society?

options.A: Missionary parish health outposts

options.D: Private commercial health agencies

question: How should a nurse respond when a client expresses fear that an IUD will cause permanent infertility?

question: Which of these is NOT a good safety practice for emergency equipment?

question: A community health nurse wants to introduce family planning in a conservative village where husbands oppose it. What is the best initial step?

question: A community nurse notices women in a village avoiding breast screening due to cultural fears. What is the best way to handle this?

question: How do non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) help relieve pain?

question: How do teenagers normally show they are trying to be more independent from their parents?

question: How does the World Health Organization define an unsafe abortion?

question: What happens to the endometrium (lining of the uterus) when pregnancy does not happen?

question: What must you ensure before sending an emergency obstetric patient on a long ambulance ride?

question: Why do nurses need to be extra careful when giving IV fluids or blood products?

question: Which of these conditions is an example of a functional (rather than structural) birth defect?

question: What official list guides healthcare workers on which medicines are approved for public health facilities?

question: Why must nurses be extra careful when giving psychiatric drugs to patients with brain degeneration?

question: A village has no local markets, poor farming land, and high unemployment. What health issue is most likely to spike here?

question: What does 'ring-fencing' mean when managing DRF finances?

question: What is the most important safety check before sending a patient for an MRI scan?

question: Why should a nurse gently rotate a PEG tube during routine stoma care?

question: Which intervention involves threading a catheter through blood vessels to block the bleeding site with tiny coils?

question: Which of these is NOT a common cause of high potassium (hyperkalemia)?

question: A 17-year-old girl is worried she will forget to take a daily pill. Which contraceptive option fits her lifestyle best?

question: Why is electrical muscle stimulation sometimes used during physical rehabilitation?

question: What is a windshield survey in community nursing?

question: Which event is most likely to trigger psychosocial stress in an older adult?

question: Which structure does the stapes bone press against to send fluid waves straight into the cochlea?

question: Why are structured handovers so important on a nursing ward?

options.B: They prevent critical patient details from being missed

question: Why does the rest of the baby's body slide out so quickly once the shoulders are born?

question: A patient asks why their new medicine isn't making them feel better right away, even though the doctor says it's working. What should you tell them?

question: If a patient's lab report shows a dangerously abnormal potassium level, which body system is at the highest immediate risk?

question: What happens when families treat reproductive health as a strictly taboo subject?

options.C: Adolescents seek out answers from peers and media, which can be inaccurate

question: Why is mixing minor tranquilizers with alcohol so dangerous?

question: What is the main goal of post-abortion care (PAC) in the ward?

question: Why is it so important to rinse the hair thoroughly after shampooing?

question: A fasting blood sugar test is most commonly used to check for which condition?

question: What shape is an intrauterine device (IUD)?

question: A dying patient is struggling to catch their breath and looks very anxious. What simple, comforting action should the nurse take first?

question: How does severe dehydration usually trick the numbers on a patient's blood lab results?

question: How do cells release stored peptide hormones into the fluid outside the cell?

question: What is the best first step for a nurse assessing a suspected victim of forced marriage?

question: What is the main difference between an antiseptic and a disinfectant?

options.C: Disinfectants are safe to drink, while antiseptics are strictly for external wounds.
options.D: Disinfectants kill viruses, while antiseptics only kill bacteria and fungi.

question: In what order should you assess a patient's abdomen during a physical exam?

options.A: Inspect, then palpate, then auscultate
options.B: Inspect, then auscultate, then palpate
options.C: Auscultate, then palpate, then inspect
options.D: Palpate, then inspect, then auscultate

explanation: Always listen (auscultate) before you press (palpate)! If you press first, you might push things around and change the natural bowel sounds. Smart nursing practice! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which quick bedside test checks for low calcium by tapping gently on the facial nerve?

options.A: Chvostek's sign
options.B: Brudzinski's sign
options.C: Homan's sign
options.D: Trousseau's sign

explanation: That's Chvostek's sign! Tap right on the cheek/facial nerve; if calcium is too low, the facial muscles will twitch uncontrollably. A classic physical assessment trick! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T3#GNS222_U2_T3_h7)

question: A patient wants to enter an SNF simply because they feel lonely at home and need help cooking meals. Why might this admission be delayed or denied coverage?

options.A: Social workers are not allowed to review home situations
options.B: The patient lacks a need for daily skilled nursing or therapy services
options.C: Medicare covers custodial care for anyone requesting it
options.D: The facility only accepts patients with infectious diseases

explanation: SNF coverage is meant for active medical or therapy needs, rather than basic social support or housekeeping help. Makes total sense! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h3)

question: Why is knowing a drug's class super helpful when you meet an unfamiliar medication on the ward?

options.A: It tells the nurse the exact room temperature for storing the drug
options.B: It guarantees the patient will not experience any adverse reactions
options.C: It gives immediate clues about expected effects and side effects
options.D: It eliminates the need to check the hospital dosage calculations

explanation: Drugs in the same family share similar actions and side effects. Once you know the class, you already know a lot about how it behaves! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T4#GNS125_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is it super important for a nurse researcher to clearly define their study population?

options.A: It ensures that every person in the country gets surveyed
options.B: It eliminates all possible errors in data collection
options.C: It reduces the financial cost of printing research papers
options.D: It helps them know exactly who the final study results will apply to

explanation: Spot on! When you know your exact population, you can proudly say who your findings will help in everyday hospital or community practice. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T16#GNS224_U1_T16_h1)

question: A nurse discovers that a struggling patient in the ward cannot buy their prescribed antibiotics. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Advocate for the patient by contacting the social welfare unit for an exemption
options.B: Reprimand the patient for coming to the hospital without money
options.C: Ignore the situation because financial matters are outside nursing duties
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately from the hospital ward

explanation: You nailed it! As patient advocates, nurses bridge the gap by connecting vulnerable patients with social welfare so they can get their meds without delay. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h8)

question: What does a serum ferritin blood test tell the healthcare team?

options.A: Circulating blood sugar
options.B: Active vitamin B12 levels
options.C: Red blood cell lifespan
options.D: Stored iron reserves

explanation: Think of ferritin as the body's iron savings account. A serum ferritin test lets you see how much iron is safely tucked away in storage. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h4)

question: Where do microfilariae mainly travel and live in the human body?

options.A: Inside liver tissue permanently
options.B: Major arteries only
options.C: Skin and subcutaneous tissues
options.D: Cerebrospinal fluid

explanation: Unlike some parasites that hang out strictly in the blood, these little ones love to migrate through your skin and tissues, setting off local immune reactions. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T7#GNS214_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the term when a brain injury causes a client to completely ignore one entire side of their body or room?

options.A: Apraxia
options.B: Unilateral neglect
options.C: Global amnesia
options.D: Expressive aphasia

explanation: Unilateral neglect can feel baffling to the client—their brain literally forgets that one side of the world (or their own body) exists. As nurses, we help bridge that gap! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T22#GNS222_U3_T22_h5)

question: What term describes the physical need for higher doses of a drug to get the same effect?

options.A: Tolerance
options.B: Intoxication
options.C: Withdrawal
options.D: Dependence

explanation: Tolerance happens when the body gets used to a drug, requiring larger amounts to produce the original feeling. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h1)

question: What is a common argument progressive religious leaders use to discourage FGM?

options.A: Science proves that cutting actually reduces female fertility
options.B: Federal tax laws require religious houses to condemn the act
options.C: The practice is just a cultural tradition, not a divine religious requirement
options.D: International groups will shut down churches and mosques that allow it

explanation: Well done! Clerics often succeed by separating true religious teachings from harmful cultural customs that have no basis in sacred texts. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T7#GNS312_U1_T7_h6)

question: How can severe kidney problems in an expectant mother directly hurt her baby?

options.A: By passing high levels of urea directly into the fetal stomach
options.B: By reducing blood supply and nutrient delivery across the placenta
options.C: By triggering early closure of the fetal cardiac chambers
options.D: By increasing the amount of amniotic fluid to dangerous levels

explanation: When the mother's kidneys and blood pressure struggle, the placenta doesn't get enough blood flow, which means the baby gets less of what it needs to grow strong. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T007#GNS226_U4_T007_h3)

question: What happens to the fetal skull bones after the baby is delivered and moulding is no longer needed?

options.A: They remain permanently overlapped until the child reaches toddler age
options.B: They fuse together immediately to protect the brain from outside injury
options.C: They gradually return to their normal shape as the pressure is relieved
options.D: They separate permanently and require surgical correction in the nursery

explanation: Because the skull bones are flexible and joined by elastic tissue, the head regains its normal rounded appearance shortly after birth. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h2)

question: What was the main drive behind early caregiving in ancient and medieval times?

options.A: Securing high financial profit
options.B: Religious duty and humanitarian support
options.C: Earning formal university degrees
options.D: Meeting government licensing requirements

explanation: Great job! Long before professional licenses and paychecks, early caregivers were driven by faith and a deep moral duty to help the vulnerable. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why do you listen with a stethoscope (auscultate) before pressing on the tummy (palpate) during an abdominal exam?

options.A: Palpation can trigger bowel movements and change the sounds you hear
options.B: Patients find palpation relaxing before listening
options.C: Auscultation is always a faster procedure
options.D: Doctors require notes in that specific order

explanation: Great catch! Pressing on the tummy first wakes up the bowels and makes them noisy, which messes up your listening assessment. Always listen first! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h1)

question: What is 'post-obstructive diuresis' after getting a catheter?

options.A: A sudden total stop in urine production caused by kidney failure
options.B: An infection caused by bacteria entering the open urinary tract
options.C: A painful spasm of the bladder muscles around the catheter
options.D: A temporary phase where the kidneys produce a massive amount of urine

explanation: Once the blockage is gone, the kidneys can overcompensate for a bit and flush out lots of fluid. You're learning real hospital scenarios! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h6)

question: What clinical sign typically tells the clinician that the uterine cavity is successfully emptied during MVA?

options.A: The syringe plunger automatically pushes itself back
options.B: The patient falls into a deep sleep
options.C: Fluid turns completely clear without any blood bubbles
options.D: Bright red foam appears and a gritty feeling is sensed

explanation: When tissue is cleared, the canula comes into contact with the empty uterine wall, producing a characteristic gritty sound or feel along with red foam in the tubing. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h5)

question: What is the very first thing the nursing team must do if a swab count doesn't add up?

options.A: Ignore the discrepancy if only one small gauze is missing
options.B: Discharge the patient and file an incident report later
options.C: Inform the surgeon immediately and halt closure
options.D: Wait until the patient wakes up to ask them

explanation: Never keep quiet about a wrong count! Alert the surgeon right away so nobody gets closed up with an extra item inside. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h5)

question: A rural health clinic in Nigeria runs out of basic antibiotics due to weak local distribution. Which national strategy is failing in this specific instance?

options.A: The regulation of surgical equipment manufacturing standards
options.B: The curriculum used to train primary school teachers
options.C: The Essential Drug Policy supply chain and distribution network
options.D: The enforcement of international luxury hotel taxation

explanation: Stockouts at rural clinics highlight flaws in the procurement and distribution mechanisms outlined by the national drug policy. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which skin layer contains the blood vessels, nerve endings, and collagen fibers?

options.A: Dermis
options.B: Hypodermis
options.C: Stratum corneum
options.D: Epidermis

explanation: The dermis is the vascularized middle layer of the skin that holds blood vessels, nerves, and tough connective tissue fibers. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h3)

question: What do we call the 'incubation period' of an infectious disease?

options.A: The time between exposure to the pathogen and the appearance of symptoms
options.B: The period before any risk factors for the disease are present
options.C: The duration when a patient experiences severe clinical fever
options.D: The time it takes for a patient to fully recover after treatment

explanation: Correct! It is the quiet period after catching a germ before you actually start feeling or showing any signs of sickness. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T13#GNS313_U1_T13_h4)

question: Why is good lighting so important when checking a patient's skin?

options.A: To accurately observe subtle changes in color and moisture
options.B: To prevent the patient from feeling nervous during the exam
options.C: To warm up the skin surface before touching it
options.D: To make the physical examination finish much faster

explanation: Great lighting is your best friend! It helps you spot tiny color shifts and moisture levels so you never miss a detail. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T8#GNS213_U5_T8_h1)

question: A community nurse visits a home with toddlers and spots an unsafe setup. Which finding needs urgent health teaching?

options.A: Hot cups of tea left sitting right near the edge of the dining table
options.B: A working smoke alarm tested and logged on the kitchen wall
options.C: Chemical cleaners stored high up in a locked utility closet
options.D: Pot handles turned inward toward the back of the stove surface

explanation: Spot on! Hot mugs near table edges are a huge scald trap for toddlers who love to reach up and pull things over. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h7)

question: In the toxicokinetic process known as ADME, what does the letter 'M' stand for?

options.A: Mobility
options.B: Mutagenesis
options.C: Metabolism
options.D: Maintenance

explanation: You're doing great! ADME stands for Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, and Excretion. It simply describes the journey a chemical takes inside the human body. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h3)

question: When measuring for a nasogastric tube using the NEX method, what does the letter 'E' stand for?

options.A: Earlobe
options.B: Epiglottis
options.C: Esophagus
options.D: Eyebrow

explanation: NEX stands for Nose to Earlobe to Xiphoid process. It's the classic bedside trick to guess how far the tube needs to go! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h4)

question: A glass bottle of lab specimen drops and shatters on the floor, creating a large spill. What should you do first?

options.A: Cover the glass shards with a cloth sheet
options.B: Leave the room and wait for the housekeeping staff to notice
options.C: Put on appropriate PPE and obtain a designated spill kit
options.D: Mop the floor quickly with a dry paper towel

explanation: Spot on! Safety first: always wear your PPE before dealing with broken glass and body fluids to protect yourself from exposure. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h7)

question: What is the main job of a Governing Board in a public health corporation?

options.A: Providing direct bedside nursing care to patients
options.B: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs locally
options.C: Setting broad policy and overseeing financial management
options.D: Writing international health treaties

explanation: Well done! The board doesn't do bedside nursing; instead, they steer the ship by setting big goals and making sure finances are properly managed. [learn more](GST321_U10_T2#GST321_U10_T2_h3)

question: What key details must be included when writing a family planning referral note?

options.A: A detailed financial breakdown of the hospital delivery bill
options.B: The baby's exact birth weight recorded in ounces and pounds
options.C: Relevant obstetric history and the specific reason for referral
options.D: The nurse's personal home address and phone contact details

explanation: The receiving clinic needs a clear picture of the mother's health history and why she was sent so they can give her the best care. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h6)

question: How often should essential emergency equipment like crash carts be checked on a hospital ward?

options.A: Every shift
options.B: Once a month
options.C: Only after a patient codes
options.D: Once a year

explanation: Routine shift checks ensure that emergency items are present, functional, and ready for immediate use. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is a key post-procedure instruction for a patient who received intravenous contrast dye during an MRI?

options.A: Avoid eating solid foods for the rest of the day
options.B: Take a strong diuretic medication immediately
options.C: Remain on complete bed rest for the next 24 hours
options.D: Drink plenty of fluids to help flush the contrast out

explanation: Increasing fluid intake helps the kidneys clear the contrast agent safely from the body. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h6)

question: What is the key difference between active and passive infection surveillance?

options.A: Active surveillance only occurs at night, while passive surveillance happens during morning shifts
options.B: Active surveillance involves staff proactively hunting for data, while passive relies on voluntary reporting
options.C: Passive surveillance tracks viral illnesses, while active surveillance focuses only on bacterial issues
options.D: Passive surveillance uses computer software, while active surveillance is done entirely on paper

explanation: Spot on! Active means staff actively go looking for cases, while passive means waiting for someone to report them. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h3)

question: Who is considered an 'informal caregiver' in elderly care?

options.A: Trainee medical students completing clinical rotations
options.B: Unpaid family members and friends who provide daily support
options.C: Hospital volunteers who visit patients on weekends
options.D: Licensed nurses who work part-time in nursing homes

explanation: Informal caregivers are usually loving relatives or friends who look after an older adult at home without getting paid. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T7#GNS321_U3_T7_h6)

question: To help prevent Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia (VAP), at what angle should the head of the patient's bed be kept?

options.A: 60 to 90 degrees upright
options.B: 30 to 45 degrees
options.C: 15 degrees slightly tilted
options.D: 0 degrees completely flat

explanation: Keeping the bed elevated between 30 and 45 degrees uses gravity to stop oral and stomach secretions from trickling down into the lungs. An easy intervention with a huge payoff! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h6)

question: Why is community involvement considered essential for the success of school health programmes?

options.A: It completely removes the financial burden from the government
options.B: It ensures that health habits taught in school are reinforced at home
options.C: It gives community leaders the legal power to hire and fire teachers
options.D: It stops students from falling sick during examination periods

explanation: When communities are involved, healthy practices do not stop at the school gate but continue inside the family environment. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h1)

question: What is the main surgical option used to treat severe stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: Widening the urethral opening with a stent
options.B: Placing a supportive sling under the urethra
options.C: Implanting an artificial kidney to filter urine
options.D: Removing the lower portion of the bladder

explanation: A surgical sling acts like a little hammock or seatbelt underneath the urethra to keep it from dropping when you move. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h7)

question: What is the first step when preparing to share serious news using the SPIKES protocol?

options.A: Setting up a private, quiet space with minimal interruptions
options.B: Giving the patient all test results immediately upon entering
options.C: Asking the family to leave the room for privacy
options.D: Reading the patient's vital signs out loud

explanation: The first step of SPIKES focuses on setting, which involves arranging a private, comfortable environment for the discussion. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h4)

question: What does finding chorioamnionitis on a delivered placenta tell you?

options.A: Maternal gestational hypertension
options.B: A normal physiological aging process of the placenta
options.C: An intrauterine bacterial infection of the fetal membranes
options.D: A previous cesarean section scar

explanation: Chorioamnionitis means bacteria got into the amniotic sac, which is a red flag that both mum and baby need to be watched closely for signs of infection. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h5)

question: Uric acid is a waste product left over when your body breaks down which of these?

options.A: Glucose
options.B: Lipids
options.C: Purines
options.D: Proteins

explanation: Spot on! Purines are natural compounds broken down by the body into uric acid, which your kidneys then work to filter out. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h2)

question: How do residential care homes differ basically from nursing homes?

options.A: Nursing homes feature 24-hour medical staff for complex health needs, while residential care focuses on daily living assistance
options.B: Residential care homes are operated by the government, while nursing homes are private
options.C: Residential care homes are exclusively for children, whereas nursing homes are strictly for the elderly
options.D: Nursing homes do not provide meals, unlike standard residential care facilities

explanation: Spot on! The big difference is clinical staffing: nursing homes have 24-hour medical care for heavy health needs, while residential homes focus more on daily living support. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T12#GNS324_U5_T12_h1)

question: What do we call those tiny, pinpoint red or purple spots caused by tiny bleeding vessels under the skin?

options.A: Petechiae
options.B: Pustules
options.C: Macules
options.D: Vesicles

explanation: Petechiae are those little pinpoint spots that show up when tiny blood vessels (capillaries) leak a bit of blood. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T8#GNS213_U5_T8_h4)

question: What is the standard temperature range for storing most routine vaccines in a clinic fridge?

options.A: Minus 20 degrees Celsius to minus 10 degrees Celsius
options.B: Minus 5 degrees Celsius to zero degrees Celsius
options.C: Plus 2 degrees Celsius to plus 8 degrees Celsius
options.D: Plus 15 degrees Celsius to plus 25 degrees Celsius

explanation: Commit +2°C to +8°C to memory! As a nurse managing the cold chain in your clinic, this is your golden rule for keeping vaccines potent. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T70#GNS214_U1_T70_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a routine component of a comprehensive clinical assessment for a febrile patient?

options.A: Monitoring respiratory and pulse rates
options.B: Checking the level of consciousness
options.C: Measuring daily bone mineral density
options.D: Observing skin warmth and diaphoresis

explanation: Bone density measurements are unrelated to the acute assessment of a febrile illness. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T6#GNS123_U3_T6_h5)

question: Why is a community diagnosis considered an ongoing cycle rather than a single event?

options.A: Because government funding stops after the first month
options.B: Because health needs change and progress must be evaluated
options.C: Because nurses are required to rewrite reports every week
options.D: Because community members refuse to answer questions twice

explanation: Communities change over time, and nurses must continuously evaluate whether interventions are working and what new problems have arisen. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h6)

question: In midwifery, what does the term 'foetal attitude' actually mean?

options.A: The rate of cervical dilation over a specific time period
options.B: The position of the placenta inside the lower uterine segment
options.C: The relationship of foetal body parts to one another
options.D: The emotional mood of the mother during contractions

explanation: Don't let the word 'attitude' confuse you—it simply describes how the baby's head and limbs are curled up against its trunk (usually tucked in nicely like a little ball). [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h5)

question: You notice a vaccine vial was left out on a counter at room temperature for six hours. What should you do?

options.A: Quickly place it back in the fridge so it can refreeze
options.B: Shake the vial vigorously to reactivate the active ingredients
options.C: Consult facility protocols and the cold chain manager before using it
options.D: Administer it immediately to the next patient before it warms further

explanation: Never guess with vaccines! Check your hospital's policy or speak with the cold chain officer first, because a warmed vaccine might need to be discarded. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T4#GNS125_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which member of the palliative team usually helps families navigate money troubles and community resources?

options.A: Social worker
options.B: Pharmacist
options.C: Surgeon
options.D: Physical therapist

explanation: You're right! Palliative social workers are lifesavers when it comes to connecting families with financial aid, support groups, and community resources. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h7)

question: What do we call positive, exciting stress that motivates you to do your best?

options.A: Distress
options.B: Eustress
options.C: Allostasis
options.D: Homeostasis

explanation: Not all stress is bad! Eustress is that healthy, exciting kind of stress—like feeling pumped before a big nursing exam or presentation. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h3)

question: What is a major focus of modern critical care nursing alongside managing advanced technology?

options.A: Discharging patients within twenty-four hours of admission
options.B: Holistic care, managing pain, and preventing ICU delirium
options.C: Limiting family involvement to reduce room contamination
options.D: Focusing entirely on machine maintenance and calibration

explanation: While machines keep patients alive, modern nurses focus heavily on human comfort, psychological well-being, and family support. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why is gender equity often necessary before gender equality can be truly achieved?

options.A: Equity provides tailored support to overcome existing social disadvantages
options.B: Equality is harmful and should be replaced entirely by equity
options.C: Equity means treating all patients with the exact same standard protocol
options.D: Equity ensures that biological sex differences are completely erased

explanation: Because historical inequalities put certain groups behind, equity steps in with customized help so everyone has a fair chance to reach an equal outcome. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why can myocarditis lead to signs of heart failure?

options.A: Heart valves become completely stuck open by fibrous scar tissue.
options.B: Electrical impulses travel too fast through the damaged heart chambers.
options.C: Inflammation damages the heart muscle cells, reducing their ability to contract effectively.
options.D: Fluid builds up inside the pericardial sac and crushes the coronary arteries.

explanation: When the heart muscle (myocardium) is inflamed, it gets tired and weak, losing its strong pumping power. This causes blood to back up—leading to heart failure symptoms. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h3)

question: A nurse is arguing loudly with a doctor at the nursing station. What type of conflict is this?

options.A: Intragroup conflict
options.B: Intrapersonal conflict
options.C: Interpersonal conflict
options.D: Organizational conflict

explanation: Anytime two or more distinct people are clashing or disagreeing, that's an interpersonal conflict. You'll see this often on the wards, and it's a great chance to practice good communication! [learn more](GST321_U5_T1#GST321_U5_T1_h2)

question: Which childhood lymphoma is very common in malaria-endemic regions like Nigeria?

options.A: Multiple myeloma
options.B: Chronic myeloid leukemia
options.C: Burkitt lymphoma
options.D: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia

explanation: Burkitt lymphoma is well-known in tropical Africa. It's often linked with the Epstein-Barr virus and chronic exposure to malaria. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T9#GNS311_U2_T9_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of regulatory bodies like the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria?

options.A: To manage the commercial business accounts of private hospitals
options.B: To protect the public by ensuring safe and competent nursing practice
options.C: To manufacture pharmaceutical drugs for local distribution
options.D: To decide which political party wins national health elections

explanation: Spot on! Professional councils exist primarily to keep the public safe by setting high educational and ethical standards for all practicing nurses. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is the main advantage of using a second messenger system like cAMP?

options.A: It stops the target cell from responding too quickly
options.B: It prevents hormones from ever leaving the bloodstream
options.C: It greatly amplifies the initial hormonal signal
options.D: It allows the hormone to physically enter the nucleus

explanation: A single hormone molecule binding outside can trigger the production of many second messengers, multiplying the cell's response. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T9#GNS211_U1_T9_h3)

question: Why do doctors need specific serological tests in addition to routine liver enzyme tests?

options.A: Routine enzymes cannot detect jaundice, whereas serological tests measure skin pigment
options.B: Liver enzymes show that injury is happening, but serological tests identify the exact viral cause
options.C: Serological tests are the only way to measure how much urine the patient is producing daily
options.D: Blood enzymes only work for Hepatitis A, requiring serological tests for all other diseases

explanation: Spot on! Routine liver tests tell us the liver is angry and inflamed, but serological blood tests act like detectives to tell us *which* specific virus started the fire. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h5)

question: What particle size is generally needed for medication to reach the deep lower airways and alveoli?

options.A: Between 50 and 100 micrometers
options.B: Greater than 20 micrometers
options.C: Between 1 and 5 micrometers
options.D: Any visible dust particle size

question: What is a healthy way for a nurse to handle heavy emotional stress during a mass casualty incident?

options.A: Working through all breaks to prove dedication to the unit
options.B: Suppressing all emotions until retirement from nursing
options.C: Taking short rotation breaks and debriefing with colleagues
options.D: Avoiding all communication with fellow staff members

explanation: Exactly! Talking with teammates and taking quick breathers helps release built-up stress so you can stay strong for your patients. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h6)

question: How do bile salts help your body digest fats?

options.A: Breaking large fat globules into tiny emulsified droplets
options.B: Releasing digestive enzymes directly into the fat droplets

question: What are the coarse hairs located inside the nasal vestibule called?

question: What is the main goal of food hygiene and safety practices?

options.C: To make cooking faster in large kitchens
options.D: To cut down the cost of buying ingredients

options.D: Using gloves only when blood is visibly dripping
